answers.stem_only: When every record in a weighted group is unhealthy, Route 53 treats them all as healthy and keeps returning them, which is why users got the failed addresses. Route 53 first considers only nonzero-weight records, and falls back to zero-weight records only when all nonzero-weight records are unhealthy. So the smallest change is to add one more weighted alias record for www.example.com that points to the S3 website endpoint (the bucket name matches the record name) with weight 0, and keep the three health-checked records as they are. A failover pair over the weighted set would also work but needs renaming and more records.

Use ELB health checks on the Auto Scaling groups so that Auto Scaling replaces instances the load balancer reports as unhealthy. For Regional failover, create Route 53 failover alias records: primary alias to the us-east-1 ALB with Evaluate Target Health set to Yes, secondary alias to the us-west-2 ALB. No scripts are needed.

The ALB's IP addresses change as it scales, so a hard-coded A record goes stale. Replace it with a Route 53 alias record (type A) that targets the ALB: Route 53 follows the current addresses, and queries to alias records that point to an ELB load balancer are not charged, which beats a CNAME (charged per query) for millions of queries. An ALB cannot take Elastic IP addresses.
